summary:
West Kalimantan has no separate legislation or enforcement record addressing LGBTI people, and no provincial authority has been documented applying distinct rules on sexual orientation or gender identity. The national legal framework of Indonesia therefore governs what a trans visitor encounters in the province.

No province-specific reporting on policing practice, facilities, care access, document handling or partner recognition in West Kalimantan was identified.
tangentialFactors: Because no provincial instrument on morality or public decency specific to LGBTI people exists in West Kalimantan, there is no sub-national penalty scale, enforcement body or court practice to assess separately. Any action against a trans visitor in the province would proceed under Indonesia's national criminal and pornography provisions, which are set out under the national entry.
localsOnly: Transgender residents of West Kalimantan stand in the same national legal position as visitors. No provincial anti-discrimination protection, complaint body or gender-recognition procedure operates at province level, and no province-specific data on employment, health care or violence affecting transgender residents was identified.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: whether any district-level morality regulations operate within West Kalimantan, and how they are applied, is not sourced. Arrest or prosecution figures for the province disaggregated by gender identity are not available.

National-level findings, including the penal code, the pornography statute, broadcasting rules, sex-marker policy and the absence of anti-discrimination protection, are set out under Indonesia's national entry and are not repeated here.
